messages.subject: Different scales
parts:
Hi,

I am using the next code to create a boxplot but I would like to know how could I select the colors and how could I use one scale until value 1 and how to use another scale after 1 (as you can see in the picture attached).

Thanks,
Ibon

setwd("D:/Boxplot")

x<-read.csv2("Froga.csv",header=T)

library(ggplot2)

pl <- qplot(Localizacion, SIR, fill=factor(Non), data=x, geom="boxplot", position="dodge")  +
  theme_bw() + coord_flip() +geom_hline(yintercept=as.numeric("1"))
print(pl)

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Different scales
parts:
What function defines that scale, and what is its inverse function?

You'll need to use the scales package and write your own scale
function. See http://blog.ggplot2.org/ and look for Brian Diggs' post
on defining your own scale (third entry from the top). You haven't
given us enough information to be able to help you along in that
endeavor.

In the group archives is a recent thread re how to define a
biexponential scale, to which Brian provided a clever solution. It
shows all the necessary steps involved in the process, including
checks that it works as intended:
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!searchin/ggplot2/biexponential$20scale/ggplot2/7ddCyXGlKiM/w3I3DWTPozMJ

BTW, if you have a question unrelated to an existing thread, please
start a new one so that in the future, those with similar inquiries
will be able to find it easily by searching the list archives.

Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Different scales
parts:
Hi:

Does this do what you want?

qplot(Localizacion, SIR, fill=factor(Non), data=x,
geom="boxplot", position="dodge") +
theme_bw() +
coord_flip() +

geom_hline(yintercept=as.numeric("1")) +
scale_y_continuous(trans = log_trans(base = 5),
breaks = seq(0.8, 1.1, by = 0.1))

The result doesn't look very different from a linear scale in your
example because of the range of the data.

Dennis
